# crumbs

> Read what a running Flutter app captured from an LLM agent or a CI script: HTTP traffic, logs, uncaught exceptions, debug dumps, in-app events, gate checks, database queries, cache operations and frame timings, held in in-memory ring buffers with an optional redacted JSONL timeline on disk, served as `crumbs_*` MCP tools and `crumbs:*` CLI commands on the `dowel` substrate. Inspired by Laravel Telescope.

**Stack**: Dart >=3.13, Flutter >=3.47. A `dowel` plugin: `CrumbsDowelProvider` adds the `crumbs:*` commands and `crumbs_*` MCP tools, which call `ext.crumbs.*` VM Service extensions inside the app. Production dependencies: `dowel`, `logging`, `meta`. Install only outside release builds.

**Setup**:

```bash
flutter pub add crumbs
dart run crumbs crumbs:install        # scaffolds ./bin/dowel, registers the plugin, patches lib/main.dart
dart run crumbs mcp:install           # the `dowel` entry in .mcp.json
./bin/dowel start --device=chrome     # or macos, linux, windows, a device id
./bin/dowel crumbs:tail               # "No log records." on a fresh start is not an error
```

```dart
import 'package:crumbs/crumbs.dart';
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart' show kDebugMode;
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

void main() {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  if (kDebugMode) {
    CrumbsPlugin.install();
    CrumbsPlugin.registerWatcher(ExceptionWatcher());
    CrumbsPlugin.registerWatcher(DumpWatcher());
  }

  runApp(const Placeholder()); // your app
}
```

## API

- `CrumbsPlugin.install()`: registers the `ext.crumbs.*` extensions and installs `LogWatcher`, which listens on `Logger.root.onRecord` and sets `Logger.root.level` to `Level.ALL`. Idempotent; call it before `runApp` (before `Magic.init` on a Magic app). `--dart-define=CRUMBS_DISABLE=1` skips it.
- `CrumbsPlugin.registerWatcher(CrumbsWatcher)`: installs a watcher at once. Shipped: `ExceptionWatcher` (chains `FlutterError.onError` and `PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError`), `DumpWatcher` (chains `debugPrint`; a no-op outside debug builds unless `allowInRelease`), `FramePerfWatcher` (frame timings and timeline block attribution).
- `CrumbsPlugin.registerHttpAdapter(CrumbsHttpAdapter)`: an HTTP capture adapter; `CrumbsStore.pendingHttpCount` sums each adapter's `pendingCount`. `DioHttpAdapter` installs no interceptor: an app's own Dio interceptor calls `DioHttpAdapter.recordRequest(...)`.
- `CrumbsStore`: the ring buffers. `recordX`, `recentX({limit})`, the `onXRecord` broadcast streams, `setCapacity(cap, kind: CrumbsKind.x)` (500 per buffer by default, frame perf 3600), `clear()`, `pause()`, `resume()`.
- `CrumbsRedaction`: credential masking of HTTP records (`hideRequestHeaders`, `hideRequestParameters`, `hideResponseParameters`, `redactParameters`, `redactBody`) and the host text hook `redactor`.
- `CrumbsFileSink.start(directory:, maxFileBytes:, maxFiles:)`: the rotating JSONL timeline of redacted log, event and exception records.
- `CrumbsDowelProvider` and `followCursor` (`package:crumbs/cli.dart`): the provider dowel loads from `lib/app/_plugins.g.dart`, and the polling loop behind `--follow`.
- `MagicCrumbsIntegration.install()` (`package:magic_devtools/crumbs.dart`): the Magic HTTP adapter and the model, cache, event, gate and query watchers, after `Magic.init()`. Available only with a `magic_devtools` release built on crumbs; otherwise `crumbs:install` warns and skips it. Until that release ships, `MagicTelescopeIntegration` feeds `fluttersdk_telescope`, not crumbs, so the HTTP, event, gate, query and cache buffers of crumbs stay empty in a Magic app.
- MCP tools: `crumbs_tail` (logs, reads `ext.crumbs.console`), `crumbs_requests`, `crumbs_exceptions`, `crumbs_dumps`, `crumbs_events`, `crumbs_gates`, `crumbs_queries`, `crumbs_caches`, `crumbs_frames`, `crumbs_clear`.
- CLI commands mirror the tools by name, except: `crumbs_exceptions` has no command, and `crumbs:install` and `crumbs:files` (the timeline files) have no tool.

## Platforms

Any Flutter target that exposes a VM Service in a debug or profile build: Android, iOS, web, macOS, Windows and Linux. `CrumbsFileSink` writes through `dart:io`, so it needs a native target; on web `start` throws. `crumbs:install` guards with `kDebugMode`, so profile and release builds drop crumbs; write `!kReleaseMode` by hand to keep profile builds.

## Rules for agents

- Crumbs reads, it never drives. Exercise the app first (tapir, a test script or a person), then read what it recorded.
- An empty buffer is not a quiet app until its producer is known to be registered: logs need `package:logging` calls, exceptions need `ExceptionWatcher`, dumps need `DumpWatcher` in a debug build, HTTP needs an adapter, events, gates, queries and caches need the Magic watchers, frames need `FramePerfWatcher`. The CLI's empty-buffer warning names the missing producer.
- Records come oldest first, the newest last. Without `since`, `limit` keeps the newest N.
- Zero the buffers with `crumbs_clear` before a repro; do not clear when chasing a fault that already happened.
- Page logs and events with the `cursor` each read returns, passed back as `since` (CLI: `--since`, or `--follow` to keep polling). A `since` that is not an integer is refused, never ignored.
- `********` is crumbs' credential mask, not the app's value. A host `redactor` that throws drops the record, so a missing line after a sensitive log call can mean a failing redactor.
- Exceptions are uncaught ones only; a swallowed `try`/`catch` shows up only if the code logged it.
- Magic model events go to the model buffer, which no extension, tool or command serves; `crumbs_events` holds auth, database and gate-definition events.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/index.md): the overview of adding crumbs and wiring the watchers
- [Installation](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/installation.md): requirements, `crumbs:install`, the build-mode guard, MCP wiring
- [Quickstart](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): from a fresh Flutter project to a first captured record
- [Buffers](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/buffers.md): the ring buffers, their capacities and eviction
- [Redaction](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/redaction.md): credential masking and the host `redactor`
- [File sink](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/file-sink.md): the JSONL timeline on disk and how to read it back
- [Watchers](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/watchers/index.md): what each watcher and adapter captures and how to register it
- [FramePerfWatcher](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/watchers/frames.md): frame timings, block attribution and the liveness counter
- [MCP overview](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/mcp/overview.md): how the crumbs tools join dowel's MCP server
- [MCP setup](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/mcp/setup.md): the `.mcp.json` entry and the reconnect
- [MCP tool reference](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/mcp/tool-reference.md): input schema and response for every `crumbs_*` tool
- [Cursor and filters](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/mcp/cursor-and-filters.md): `since`, `cursor`, `logger` and `type` on logs and events
